PMID:21339078.topic: Primary total hip arthroplasty quality indicators
PMID:21339078.setting: Servicio de Cirugía Ortopédica y Traumatología, Hospital Dos de Maig, Consorci Sanitari Integral, Barcelona
PMID:21339078.standard: Management indicators (hospital stay, readmission rate) and clinical practice indicators (dislocation rate, infection rate) for non-traumatic primary THA; no target stated

cycle1.result: Median (range) hospital stay 8 (7-78) days

PMID:21339078.other_findings: 160 patients in total across both audits; readmission, dislocation and infection results are not given in the supplied text. Authors conclude the audit cycle improved quality of care.

PMID:21515522.topic: Bone protection prescribing after hip fracture
PMID:21515522.setting: Southern General Hospital, Glasgow; fractured neck of femur patients with fracture liaison specialist nurse recommendations
PMID:21515522.standard: Discharge prescription should include the secondary prevention medication recommended by the fracture liaison specialist nurse

cycle1.result: Recommended secondary prevention medications included in discharge prescriptions in 50.9%

PMID:21515522.intervention: Fluorescent drug kardex stickers detailing simple treatment recommendations

cycle2.result: Recommended medications prescribed on discharge in 84.6%

EPMC:PMC:PMC8135667.setting: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics; orthopaedic trauma wards
EPMC:PMC:PMC8135667.standard: All patients admitted acutely should have a Hospital Anticipatory Care Plan (HACP) completed within 24 hours

cycle1.result: 37/50 (74%) had HACPs completed; 18/37 (49%) completed within 24 hours; median time to completion 45.3 hours (range 0.4-275.1 hours)

EPMC:PMC:PMC8135667.intervention: Staff teaching sessions and dissemination of infographic posters
EPMC:PMC:PMC8135667.other_findings: Carried out during the COVID-19 pandemic; cycle 2 completion within 24 hours is not given in the supplied text.

PMID:12661384.setting: Adult orthopaedic ward, Southern General Hospital, Glasgow

cycle1.result: 3159 bed days in total; 255 bed days (8%) blocked by 46 patients (41 emergency, 5 elective); 236 (93%) of blocked days due to emergency admissions

PMID:12661384.other_findings: Most blocked beds were patients awaiting rehabilitation in a young disabled unit or geriatric rehabilitation ward.

PMID:11207952.topic: Clinical pathway variance in joint arthroplasty
PMID:11207952.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Cairns Base Hospital, Queensland
PMID:11207952.standard: Clinical pathways for total hip and total knee arthroplasty (variance from pathway)

cycle1.result: TKR: 11 serious variances in 8/65 patients (12.3%); THR: 9 serious variances in 7/52 patients (13.5%)

PMID:11207952.other_findings: A surprisingly high number of cardiac events among TKR serious variances; serious variances higher than anticipated.

PMID:25979000.setting: Orthopaedic Department, Royal Bolton Hospital (district general hospital)
PMID:25979000.standard: Operative intervention within 36 h of admission (Best Practice Tariff / National Hip Fracture Database)

cycle1.result: Mean time to theatre 49±39 h

PMID:25979000.intervention: Two additional morning trauma lists, targeted by analysing Best Practice Tariff achievement by day of admission
PMID:25979000.other_findings: Variation by day of the week of admission was used to identify specific deficiencies in local service provision.

PMID:25989768.setting: Section of Orthopaedics, Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi; patients undergoing Austin Moore hemiarthroplasty

cycle1.result: Preoperative magnification 8%±4% (overestimation of implant size by 4.2±2.3mm); postoperative magnification 13%±4%; fixed 15% scaling correctly estimated implant size in 15 (24%) patients

PMID:25989768.other_findings: Digital pelvic radiographs showed variable and inconsistent magnification on repeat examination.

PMID:26794007.setting: Orthopaedic foot and ankle consultants in the Wessex area (Basingstoke and North Hampshire Hospital)

cycle1.result: Management of acute peroneal tendon tears varied greatly among the nine surgeons

PMID:26794007.other_findings: Questionnaire survey of surgeons; a literature-based protocol was proposed.

PMID:24162632.standard: Guideline-recommended admission from ED within four hours and operative management within 48 hours

cycle1.result: 5.6% admitted from ED within four hours; 51% operated within 48 hours

cycle2.result: 14.2% admitted from ED within four hours; 72.5% operated within 48 hours

PMID:24162632.other_findings: Lack of available theatre space accounted for 51% of delays in 2008 and remains a major cause of delayed surgery.

PMID:1588657.setting: San Diego County trauma system (Medical Audit Committee determinations)

cycle1.result: Errors identified in 4% of all trauma admissions; 5.9% of trauma deaths considered preventable or potentially preventable

PMID:1588657.other_findings: Commonest single error was failure to appropriately evaluate the abdomen; critical care errors had the greatest impact on preventable death.

PMID:15256916.topic: Bone bank allograft use and outcomes
PMID:15256916.setting: Bone bank, Department of Orthopaedics, Odense University Hospital

cycle1.result: 423 femoral heads donated to 300 patients; 7% of transplanted patients reoperated for infection (4% in hip revision group); no disease transmission

PMID:15256916.other_findings: Allografts used mainly for revision hip arthroplasty (34%) and fracture surgery (24%); use shifted from spinal fusion to hip revision and fracture surgery over the decade.

PMID:12581299.topic: Hip fracture analgesia, time to surgery and pressure ulcers
PMID:12581299.setting: Department of Orthopedics, Lund University Hospital
PMID:12581299.standard: Aims: optimise preoperative pain relief, reduce time from admission to operation and reduce pressure ulcers; no target stated

cycle1.result: Close to half waited more than 24 hours for operation; 11% operated within 12 hours; 19% had pressure ulcers at discharge

PMID:12581299.intervention: Quality improvements with attention from all staff (details not given)

cycle2.result: 34% waited more than 24 hours; 24% operated within 12 hours; 4.5% had pressure ulcers at discharge

PMID:12581299.other_findings: Interim 1999 measurement: 36% waited more than 24 hours, 18% operated within 12 hours, 8% pressure ulcers. Patients waiting more than 1 hour for pain relief almost halved.

PMID:12215032.setting: Departments of Orthopaedics and Audit, Princess Margaret Hospital, Swindon
PMID:12215032.standard: Trust maximum surgical blood ordering schedule (MSBOS): 6 units of blood for revision hip arthroplasty

cycle1.result: 80.3% received less than 6 units, 12.2% received 6 units and 7.5% received more than 6 units

PMID:12215032.other_findings: 14 patients had postoperative Hb < 9 g/dl and needed additional units; authors suggest 4 units rather than 6 when pre-operative Hb is 13 g/dl or more.

PMID:20497730.topic: Surgical site infection rates in foot and ankle surgery
PMID:20497730.setting: Nine podiatric surgeons Australia-wide (La Trobe University Podiatry Clinic)
PMID:20497730.standard: Australian Council on Health Care Standards (ACHS) infection definitions; literature benchmark of 0.5-6.5%

cycle1.result: Overall infection rate 3.1%; infection resulting in re-admission 0.25% (1339 admissions, 2387 procedures)

PMID:20497730.other_findings: Authors report rates within accepted industry standards.

PMID:41589557.topic: Cost of surgical site infection after hip fracture
PMID:41589557.setting: Irish healthcare system, national hip fracture clinical audit data

cycle1.result: 16 (0.4%) hip fracture patients developed an SSI; total cost €712,898, mean €44,556 per patient

PMID:41589557.other_findings: Mean cost €35,418 for males and €50,039 for females; €49,712 in those aged ≥80.

PMID:18201504.setting: Department of Orthopaedics, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 18 (66.7%) questionnaires returned; 38.9% felt in-patient admission was needed for pain; 67% of those 55 and older vs 11% under 55 (P = 0.04)

PMID:18201504.other_findings: Patient age may predict need for admission after day-case arthroscopic sub-acromial decompression.

PMID:7921563.topic: Emergency department fracture management and referral
PMID:7921563.setting: Accident and Emergency Department, Kings College Hospital, London (teaching hospital)
PMID:7921563.standard: Standard of treatment as determined by fracture clinic doctors; upper limb fracture treatment and referral guidelines

cycle1.result: Some error in 69/215 (32.1%) referrals; 51/215 (23.7%) potentially liable to increased morbidity

PMID:7921563.intervention: Introduction of fracture treatment and referral guidelines in the A&E department

cycle2.result: Errors in 14/111 (12.6%); 8 patients (7.2%) at risk of increased morbidity

PMID:7921563.other_findings: Overall improvement 19.5% (95% CI 12.3 to 29.7%); 16.5% (95% CI 9.1 to 23.9%) reduction in potentially more significant errors.

PMID:21675071.topic: Transfusion and preoperative anaemia in lower limb arthroplasty
PMID:21675071.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, Fremantle Hospital, Western Australia

cycle1.result: Overall transfusion 16.0%; primary arthroplasty 11%; revision 44.4%; with preoperative Hb ≤120 g/l transfusion 47.7% vs 7.2% above

PMID:21675071.other_findings: Authors suggest investigating and optimising anaemia when preoperative Hb is 120 g/l or less.

PMID:21675093.standard: NICE guidance on metastatic spinal cord compression

cycle1.result: 5 (50%) had MRI within 24 hours; 6 (60%) had full MRI scan; 8 (80%) had corticosteroids before MRI; 6 (60%) had radiotherapy within 24 hours; 4 (40%) referred to orthopaedics

PMID:21675093.other_findings: Number unable to walk increased by 20% up to 14 days after confirmation; authors recommend a fast-track referral pathway and education.

PMID:9914933.setting: University of Texas Medical Branch, Galveston; reconstructive spine surgery

cycle1.result: Autologous red cells made up 87% of blood transfused in sequestration patients (80) and 49% in autotransfusion-only patients (302)

PMID:9914933.other_findings: Sequestration plus salvage was more cost effective than salvage alone and reduced reliance on allogeneic products.

cycle1.result: All case-mix variables strongly associated with post-operative mortality; management variables (including time to surgery) added no significant improvement to the model

PMID:22989282.setting: Tertiary care university trauma service, University of California, Irvine

cycle1.result: 25% drank more than recommended and 4% were dependent; 92% found computerised screening easy

PMID:22989282.other_findings: AUDIT here is the Alcohol Use Disorder Identification Test, not a clinical audit.

PMID:10755427.standard: Local guidelines: experienced surgeon responsible for initial management; K-wire stabilisation of type IIB and III fractures; crossed K-wires of adequate thickness (1.6 mm)

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:10755427.intervention: Guidelines proposed after the previous four-year review

cycle2.result: Guidelines followed in 52 of 71 cases; no reoperations or malunion when followed; in 19 cases not followed more than one-third needed further operation and six had varus deformity

PMID:10755427.other_findings: Failure to follow guidelines led to an unsatisfactory result in 11 patients; a management protocol was devised.

PMID:8632389.topic: Surgical site infection rates in elective orthopaedics
PMID:8632389.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Southmead Hospital, Bristol

cycle1.result: Early wound infection rate 7.85%

cycle2.result: Early wound infection rate 6.82% (no significant difference)

PMID:8632389.other_findings: 44% of infections occurred after discharge; no difference between theatres with and without laminar air flow; 35 of 53 minor infections had no microbiological specimen.

PMID:17059712.setting: Fracture clinics, Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, West Wales General Hospital, Carmarthen

cycle1.result: Overall discharge rate 38%, differing significantly between consultants

PMID:17059712.other_findings: Re-presentation rates were similar between consultants who discharged aggressively and those who re-reviewed; discharge protocols recommended.

PMID:21817000.setting: Podiatry Outpatients, Repatriation General Hospital, Daw Park, South Australia

cycle1.result: Postoperative infection rate 18.9% after excisional nail matrixectomy

PMID:21817000.other_findings: Rate compared with 0.5%-6.5% for clean foot and ankle surgery; authors raise the case for antibiotic prophylaxis.

PMID:12585629.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, West Cumberland Hospital, Whitehaven

cycle1.result: 304 out-patient visits; 10 patients needed intervention, only 3 identified at routine visits; 8 of 187 radiographs (4.3%) abnormal; minimum cost 23,297 pounds

PMID:12585629.other_findings: Authors recommend a single visit at 6-12 weeks then discharge if no problems anticipated.

PMID:10932666.setting: Trent Regional Arthroplasty Study (regional hip register), University of Leicester, Glenfield Hospital

cycle1.result: 91 different surgeons performed revisions; only two performed more than 20 per year; Charnley most commonly revised (38.3% acetabular, 37.5% femoral)

PMID:10932666.other_findings: More than 100 prosthetic combinations used; revisions performed in all hospitals with orthopaedic in-patient facilities.

PMID:7515432.topic: Primary bone tumours of the shoulder
PMID:7515432.setting: Leeds Regional Bone Tumour Registry, St James's University Hospital, Leeds

cycle1.result: 145 of 2039 cases (7%) were shoulder tumours; 75% proximal humerus, 20% scapula, 5% clavicle; 73 malignant vs 72 benign

PMID:7515432.other_findings: Registry changed the referring pathologist's diagnosis in 11 cases; correct preoperative diagnosis made only in a minority.

PMID:12782548.setting: 91 English professional football clubs (The Football Association)

cycle1.result: Ankle ligament sprains 11% of injuries; 77% lateral ligament complex; 12 138 days and 2033 matches missed

PMID:12782548.other_findings: More sprains from contact than non-contact mechanisms (59% v 39%), except in goalkeepers.

PMID:32720479.topic: Buckle fracture soft cast and discharge
PMID:32720479.setting: Emergency department, University Hospital Waterford (advanced nurse practitioners)
PMID:32720479.standard: Literature recommendation of minimalist treatment for buckle fractures

cycle1.result: Successful outcome for all 88 patients treated in a soft cast with verbal and written discharge information

PMID:32720479.intervention: Protocol change to soft cast for home removal with verbal and written discharge information and no follow-up appointment
PMID:32720479.other_findings: Avoiding return visits gave significant travel time and distance savings for families.

PMID:18796190.topic: Triage service referrals to orthopaedic clinic
PMID:18796190.setting: Lower limb orthopaedic clinic, The Royal Surrey County Hospital, Guildford (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 132 patients referred via MPTT clinic waited 140 days vs 62 days for direct GP referral

PMID:18796190.other_findings: Patient confusion over professional roles and diagnostic indecision were noted for MPTT referrals.

PMID:22593128.topic: Preoperative anaemia and transfusion in arthroplasty
PMID:22593128.setting: Airedale NHS Foundation Trust (UK general hospital); primary hip or knee arthroplasty
PMID:22593128.standard: National agency instruction to implement blood conservation measures including preoperative anaemia management

cycle1.result: Preoperative Hb predicted allogeneic blood transfusion (odds ratio 0.25 per 1 g/dl)

cycle2.result: Associated with improved outcome up to 90 days after discharge; figures not given in the supplied text

PMID:20575946.setting: Orthopaedic trauma theatre, Flinders Medical Centre
PMID:20575946.standard: Institutional standards: end utilisation 77%; operating theatre utilisation 85-90%; changeover and start times

cycle1.result: End utilisation 78.8% and operating theatre utilisation 81%; changeover and start times sub-standard

PMID:20575946.other_findings: Consistently prolonged changeovers and late starts.

PMID:14728950.topic: Early management of pelvic and acetabular fractures
PMID:14728950.setting: SW Thames regional pelvic and acetabular unit (St Peters Hospital, Chertsey)
PMID:14728950.standard: Guidelines laid down for early management in four specific areas

cycle1.result: Excess mortality in patients > 85 years tended to return to background level after two to five years; in < 85 years it persisted beyond eight years

PMID:16551419.setting: Orthopaedic unit, Stoke Mandeville Hospital; elective TKR and THR
PMID:16551419.standard: Maximum Surgical Blood Ordering Schedule (MSBOS) and national guidelines

cycle1.result: High level of unnecessary cross-matched blood; THR cross-match transfusion (C:T) ratio 3.21

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:35021026.other_findings: Evaluates six EHR-based triggers for detecting adverse events compared with self-reporting; no results given in the supplied text.

cycle1.result: 34% received surgery within 24 hours; one-year mortality 34%
